title: The Hidden Switch — How I Stopped Hating Hard Work (And Started Craving It)
hook: About Me (Past Result) — cold open on 'the best three months of work in my life last year,' before explaining the mechanism that caused it.
key_points: There are two fuel sources for motivation: extrinsic (money, praise, status, avoiding punishment) and a second, stronger one the narrator didn't know existed.
The brain gets more dopamine from wanting a reward than from getting it, so extrinsic-fuel wins go flat within days.
What reads as laziness or lack of discipline is actually a fuel-source problem, not a character problem.
PROVISIONAL — incomplete: the actual mechanism/reveal of the second fuel source, and how the narrator's daily experience changed once they switched to it, are not yet in the source script.
core_message: You are not lazy — you may just be running your motivation on the wrong fuel.
tone: Raw & Unfiltered — first-person, real-time-thinking cadence, self-interrupted, unpolished.
style: Narrated monologue / faceless YouTube explainer — motion graphics and visual-metaphor illustration over voiceover, no on-camera talent.
